title: Comparative Forms
summary: Making basic comparisons with adjectives in everyday situations.
whyItMatters: Comparatives let you choose between clothes, describe differences between people, and compare weather or objects. The core pattern is adjective plus '-er', followed by 'als' when both sides are named.

mentalModel.title: Turn up one quality
mentalModel.content: The comparative marks more of a quality: warm becomes wärmer, groß becomes größer.

mentalModel.title: Use als as the comparison bridge
mentalModel.content: When naming both sides, connect them with 'als': 'Die Jacke ist wärmer als der Pullover.'

mentalModel.title: Memorize high-frequency irregular forms
mentalModel.content: Treat gut-besser, viel-mehr, and gern-lieber as complete pairs.

ruleBlocks.title: Add -er for the comparative
ruleBlocks.content: Most short adjectives form the comparative with '-er': klein-kleiner, schnell-schneller, warm-wärmer.

ruleBlocks.title: Use als for difference
ruleBlocks.content: Name the comparison standard after 'als': 'Heute ist es kälter als gestern.'

ruleBlocks.title: Use so ... wie for equality
ruleBlocks.content: Use 'so + adjective + wie' when the quality is equal: 'Die Schuhe sind so teuer wie die Stiefel.'

ruleBlocks.title: Learn irregular comparison pairs
ruleBlocks.content: Important forms include gut-besser, viel-mehr, gern-lieber, hoch-höher, and nah-näher.

tables.title: Difference and Equality
rows: Mia ist so sportlich wie Anna.

sentenceStructure: The comparative adjective usually remains predicative and uninflected after 'sein'.
'Wie' belongs to the equality pattern 'so ... wie'.
The compared categories should be logically parallel.

concepts: use comparative adjectives inside noun phrases

comparisons.summary: The theme lesson supplies people, clothing, and weather qualities to compare.
The communication lesson uses comparisons carefully in descriptions and reactions.

examples.de: Lena ist größer als ihre Schwester.
examples.en: Lena is taller than her sister.

examples.de: Heute ist es wärmer als gestern.
examples.en: Today it is warmer than yesterday.

examples.de: Der Mantel ist teurer, aber auch wärmer.
examples.en: The coat is more expensive but also warmer.

examples.de: Die schwarze Jacke ist so bequem wie die blaue.
examples.en: The black jacket is as comfortable as the blue one.

commonMistakes.reason: Standard German uses 'als' after an unequal comparative.
Do not add 'mehr' to an adjective that already has a comparative form.

specialCases: Many one-syllable adjectives add an umlaut, but not all do.
Regional speech may use 'wie' after comparatives; standard written German uses 'als'.
Adjective endings on comparative forms are a later expansion.
tips: Learn base and comparative as a pair.
Compare two real objects using three qualities.
